ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a large shaded blue triangle with a horizontal base labeled 29 cm. Its left side is vertical, forming the height to the base. To the left of this vertical side is a dashed pink right triangle: its horizontal leg is labeled 6 cm, its slanted dashed side is labeled 13 cm, and a right-angle marker shows the vertical segment is perpendicular to the horizontal line. Reasoning: The dashed right triangle shares the same vertical height as the blue triangle. Using the Pythagorean theorem, h^2 + 6^2 = 13^2, so h = sqrt(13^2 - 6^2) = sqrt(169 - 36) = sqrt(133). The area of the blue triangle is (1/2)(base)(height) = (1/2)(29)(sqrt(133)) ≈ 167.2. Final answer: 167.2 cm².
